summary: Kozani National Airport Filippos (KZI) is a regional airport serving the city of Kozani in the Western Macedonia region of northern Greece. Named after Philip II of Macedon, the ancient king who unified the Macedonian kingdom, the airport provides an important gateway to a region rich in archaeological and natural heritage. The facility primarily handles domestic flights and seasonal charter operations, supporting both tourism and the local economy centered on agriculture and energy production.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate from Kozani National Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by Olympic Air (now part of Aegean Airlines) with regular domestic connections, mainly to Athens. Seasonal charter flights may also operate during summer months.

Q: How far is the airport from Kozani city center?
A: Kozani Airport is located approximately 8 km southeast of the city center, and the drive typically takes around 15-20 minutes depending on traffic.

Q: Does the airport operate year-round?
A: Yes, the airport operates year-round, though flight frequency may be reduced during off-peak winter seasons compared to summer.

Q: Are there international flights from Kozani?
A: International flights are limited; the airport mainly handles domestic routes, with occasional seasonal charters to European destinations during the summer tourist season.
transport_tips: Taxis are available outside the terminal and provide the most convenient transfer to Kozani city or nearby towns; pre-booking is recommended during off-peak hours when taxis may be limited. Public bus services connect the airport to Kozani city center, though schedules are infrequent. Renting a car is advisable for travelers planning to explore the wider Western Macedonia region, including Mount Vermio and the ancient site of Aigai (Vergina).
local_tip: If you have time before your flight, ask about visiting the nearby archaeological site of Aigai (modern Vergina), the ancient first capital of Macedonia where Philip II was assassinated and where his tomb and royal treasures were discovered—it's only about a 30-minute drive from the airport.
